PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 model with run_id ros-wave-c-056, reviewed_by stays null; no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no MuJoCo engine, ROS graph, Gazebo/Isaac simulator or robot run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper RosDriver (family ros), but the pinned clone contains no ROS node that implements the simulator interface; its MuJoCo path is the external mujoco_ros2_control node configured by urdf/mujoco_ros2_control.xacro:7 to load mjcf/small_warehouse.xml. The card's own candidate classes are cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1, and its mock strategy prefers the upstream simulator. The package therefore uses MujocoDriver over the configured MJCF (model_path points at the read-only clone in place; it is not copied or modified). The card lists empty_world.xml as models[0], but the configured MuJoCo model is small_warehouse.xml (xacro:7); only that scene is served, and empty_world.xml, the Gazebo/Isaac assets and the ROS 2 control layer are NOT COVERED. No Python native exists and native.py is not used.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action:{ctrl:[2 numbers]}} and cap.world.reset.v1. The bridge reads the model's actuator_ctrlrange; the two velocity actuators declare no ctrlrange (mjcf/bcr_bot.xml:148-153), so no numeric control bound is declared or invented and action_limits() is empty. The model's free joint and two wheel hinges give 9 qpos, 8 qvel and 2 ctrl entries; option timestep is 0.002 s (mjcf/bcr_bot.xml:5). World state = time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed, native_checkpoint. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served by MujocoBridge; reset's seed field is accepted but mj_resetData does not use a seed.

SAFETY: risk R0 reflects isolated simulated world stepping (MHS-004 SAFE-006); no physical mobile-base command, actuator torque, sensor stream or hardware command is exposed. The runtime's software e-stop latch blocks step and reset until mhs.safety.reset, while state remains readable; this is not a hardware e-stop and makes no physical-safety claim. No estop_physical_ref is claimed.

FAKE: the fake backend is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module, not the upstream simulator. It parses the MJCF and its includes for model shape, actuator names and option timestep and advances a placeholder state; it loads no mesh/texture/inertia/contact, resolves no friction/tendon/equality/force constraint, and uses the bridge's basic snapshot profile (time, qpos, qvel, act, ctrl; no full integration/warm-start). Fidelity is F0 with lockstep clock, no realtime pacing and the gaps listed in driver.py; the real sim backend would be the official mujoco module loading the same file, which was not installed or run. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND are the SDK's simulator-family warnings for a class-object backend; they do not mean this fake is the upstream simulator and no native call recording is claimed. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE (no limit on an actuating capability) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (ticks, action.ctrl[*], seed) are expected for MuJoCo-derived world classes per PLAYBOOK.md section 8; no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were raised. MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation, the model path, the derived shape (9 qpos, 8 qvel, 2 ctrl, 2 ms timestep), all 14 facts, the F0 stand-in fake and the R0 software-latch safe state against the pin: the clone implements no ROS node (its MuJoCo runtime is the external mujoco_ros2_control node configured by urdf/mujoco_ros2_control.xacro:4-7), the configured MJCF uses only in-clone OBJ meshes and PNG textures, the clone has no hardware path, and an in-process lockstep MuJoCo does stop advancing when the latch refuses steps, so the deviation and the safe state stand. Defects: five facts said more than their lines (a 'so ...' clause on the installed directories, judgements that the launch remap is 'not a node implemented in the clone', that the controller settings, quoted with units the YAML does not state, are 'not this package's world-step bounds' and that empty_world.xml is 'not the model selected', and a controller parameter file outside the cited range), and a sixth named the framequat sensor 'framequaternion'. The reviewer narrowed those facts, widened the launch citation to 33-54, and added two sim fidelity gaps (the scene was never compiled by MuJoCo and its rangefinder names a site inside a replicate block; the actuators declare no ctrlrange, so any finite wheel-velocity target is accepted) (driver.py); updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged; the override proposal records family mujoco. For the human reviewer: Simulation only; the package steps its own in-process MuJoCo copy of mjcf/small_warehouse.xml read in place from the clone (model_path is a relative path to robots/...), never the upstream ROS 2 graph. An MHS e-stop latches that instance only; a separately launched mujoco_ros2_control or Gazebo simulation of bcr_bot is unaffected. The real MuJoCo backend was never run: confirm the scene compiles (replicated LiDAR sites, OBJ meshes) before any sim use. Wheel-velocity ctrl is unbounded because the model declares no ctrlrange.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): SDK change MHS/changes/MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS.md: a MuJoCo model that gives no actuator a control range is no longer served silently unbounded; the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required, so the endpoint refuses a step that sets it (MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET, before the native step) until the site's overlay bounds it, G6 now exercises that refusal and the gate's G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning is gone (the conformance run probes the overlay's bound). Decision: fix, pass. Changed: site-limits.example.json (new: an illustrative -10..10 for every control, source operator, labelled example only, not a value of the model); driver.py and facts.md (the statements that a step accepts any control value or that no limit is operator_required); test_driver.py (the cases serve the example overlay; a new case shows the LIMITS_UNSET refusal without it; the shape case expects action.ctrl operator_required instead of no limit); reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json regenerated. The gate passes G1-G9 with G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND and G8.NO_UNIT x3; the digest changed from sha256:817572760504a5cf9843bf8d5fb3acf13d1f62cd91da93459f5a7021c9c51224 to sha256:70d95461c229c5746bb052914af7e7a8b30bc4c67b446bfd2a6c898b891dc76e because of this intended correction. No source in the clone states a control bound, so none is invented.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review of the reviewer edits made by claude-opus-5-5 with the SDK change MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): The model states no actuator control range; the bridge now publishes action.ctrl as operator_required instead of serving it unbounded, so a step that sets it is refused (MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET) until an operator overlay bounds it, and the text that said any value is accepted was corrected. The shipped site-limits.example.json is an example (reason starts 'example only:', issued_by operator:example), not a model bound. Illustrative -10..10. Gate passes under collect --strict with the new digest; the only finding change is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE removed. Evidence is contract_checked on the package's fake backend (MuJoCo itself was not run); this is a model review, not a human one.
